title: Robust Learning Under Distribution Shifts for Non-Stationary Data Environments
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
tldr: AHO-InDNN combines drift detection with online incremental learning and LDP-based optimization to achieve 98.74% accuracy in fraud detection under non-stationary conditions.
problem_and_motivation: Machine learning systems trained on stationary assumptions fail when data distributions evolve due to changing user behavior, new fraud strategies, or seasonal patterns. Existing approaches address drift detection, adaptive learning, or optimization in isolation, lacking integrated robust frameworks. Model uncertainty and robustness optimization remain under-explored in non-stationary financial data environments.
approach: AHO-InDNN framework integrates drift detection, online incremental learning, and Lévy-based parameter optimization for non-stationary environments.
Drift detection module uses hybrid statistical divergence and mean shift to identify sudden, gradual, and recurrent concept drift in transaction streams.
InDNN architecture with dynamic depth and neuron structure handles distribution shifts through 64 input neurons, 7 hidden layers, and 64 output neurons.
Online incremental learning updates model parameters without full retraining when distribution changes are detected.
Archerfish Hunting Optimization (AHO) balances exploration and exploitation through shooting, jumping, and Lévy flight behaviors.
LDP-based optimization measures probability of exceptional bursts in streaming data to enhance model stability and robustness.
Model evaluated on PaySim artificial mobile money transaction data under simulated concept drift scenarios.
findings: num: AHO-InDNN achieves 98.74% accuracy, 98.42% precision, 98.52% recall, and 98.37% F1-score on PaySim dataset.
num: Proposed model outperforms KNN (91.67% accuracy), SMOTEBoost (78% precision), and MH-DRNN (98.5% accuracy).
num: Model demonstrates robust performance under sudden, gradual, and recurrent drift scenarios.
num: LDP optimization effectively distinguishes normal transaction variation from fraudulent anomalies.
num: Drift-aware updates enable incremental learning when significant distribution changes are detected.
num: Lévy flight reinitialization prevents stagnation and improves adaptation under dynamic distribution shifts.
